data.name: Methionine
data.description: Essential sulfur-containing amino acid. The cell reads its supply in two ways: indirectly through its metabolite S-adenosylmethionine (SAM), which binds SAMTOR (GU2017), and, according to a 2026 chemoproteomic study in human cells (SANG2026), directly as free methionine bound by PKM2. Restricting methionine improves metabolic health and lifespan in animal models, as summarised in the review KNO2026, which is why these sensors matter for ageing research.
data.description_beginner: An essential amino acid that the body cannot make. The cell keeps track of how much it has, partly through a molecule made from it (SAM) and possibly also by sensing methionine itself.

reading_levels.beginner: An essential amino acid the cell can read directly.
reading_levels.student: Free methionine; reported by one 2026 study to be read by PKM2, separately from its metabolite SAM (read by SAMTOR).
reading_levels.research: Two methionine readouts now sit side by side: SAM-SAMTOR acting at GATOR1-KICSTOR, and free methionine-PKM2 acting at GATOR2 (SANG2026, human cells, single study). Their relative weight under dietary methionine restriction is untested.

studies.title: "Trojan" Methionine Probe Reveals PKM2 as a Methionine-Sensing Protein in the mTORC1 Pathway
studies.authors: Sang Z; Zheng Y; Wang X; Wu C; Zhao J; Wang JJ; Sui S; Wang J
studies.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Identifies PKM2 as a direct methionine sensor for mTORC1. A photoaffinity methionine analogue plus chemoproteomics showed that PKM2 binds free methionine through a distinct recognition pocket — independently of its glycolytic enzyme activity — and transduces methionine availability to mTORC1 via the GATOR2 complex. Complements SAMTOR (GU2017), which reads the methionine metabolite SAM rather than methionine itself, and suggests a route to a pharmacological "methionine pseudostarvation" state.

studies.title: SAMTOR is an S-adenosylmethionine sensor for the mTORC1 pathway
studies.authors: Gu X; Orozco JM; Saxton RA; Condon KJ; Liu GY; Krawczyk PA; Scaria SM; Harper JW; Gygi SP; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Extended nutrient sensing beyond amino acids to METABOLITES: SAMTOR reads S-adenosylmethionine (SAM), the cell's methyl-donor currency, linking methionine and one-carbon metabolism to mTORC1. Relevant to why methionine restriction affects aging.

studies.title: mTORC1 stimulates cell growth through SAM synthesis and m6A mRNA-dependent control of protein synthesis
studies.authors: Villa E; Sahu U; O'Hara BP; Ali ES; Helmin KA; Asara JM; Gao P; Singer BD; Ben-Sahra I

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: SAMTOR (GU2017) showed the cell can sense S-adenosylmethionine and report it to mTORC1. This study runs the arrow the other way: mTORC1 controls how much SAM the cell makes. Downstream of mTORC1, c-MYC binds intron 1 of MAT2A and raises expression of the enzyme that produces SAM, the cell's main methyl donor; mTORC1 separately increases the protein level of WTAP, the regulatory subunit of the m6A RNA methyltransferase complex. Together these raise m6A methylation of mRNA, which primes the translation machinery for growth. Blocking MAT2A lowers SAM, m6A, protein synthesis rate and tumor growth.

studies.title: The hallmarks of protein and amino acid restriction in aging and longevity

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Cross-species review (yeast, worm, fly, rodent, human)
studies.finding: Defines the "hallmarks" of dietary protein restriction (PR) through the lens of aging: PR and restriction of specific essential amino acids — especially methionine, isoleucine and valine — improve metabolic health, healthspan and lifespan across organisms, with amino-acid composition (not just protein quantity) acting as a key determinant via nutrient-sensing pathways including mTORC1.

relations.mechanism: Free methionine binds PKM2 in a recognition pocket separate from its catalytic site. Binding does not inhibit PKM2 as an enzyme: the sensing works independently of its glycolytic activity. What changes is PKM2's interaction with GATOR2: when methionine is present, PKM2 stops restraining GATOR2 (the restraining step is the separate PKM2-GATOR2 edge), so methionine switches that brake off. The binding was captured in living human cells with a photoaffinity methionine analogue and confirmed biochemically. This reads methionine itself, unlike SAMTOR, which reads the metabolite SAM.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Methionine sticks to PKM2. This does not switch the enzyme off; it just stops PKM2 from holding the brake on GATOR2. A second methionine detector next to SAMTOR.
relations.context: Parallel to, not a replacement for, SAM sensing by SAMTOR (SAM-SAMTOR): the two sensors read different molecules and act on different complexes (PKM2 on GATOR2, SAMTOR on GATOR1-KICSTOR). How much each contributes when methionine is restricted in a whole animal is untested.
relations.boundary: One study in cultured human cells (SANG2026): photoaffinity chemoproteomics plus biochemical validation. No affinity measurement in tissue, no animal or human test, and not yet replicated by another group. The direction (methionine binding relieves PKM2's restraint on GATOR2) is taken from the authors' abstract; the full text was not accessible when this link was written.
